key_insight: A Fitch-based wind farm parameterization in CM1 shows how turbine-induced warming and circulations can promote earlier convection initiation tens of kilometers downstream.
engineering_relevance: The implementation enables simulations of wind farm impacts on boundary layer flow and convective development beyond the farm footprint.
method: Represent turbines as elevated momentum sinks and TKE sources within the rotor-swept layer.
Optimize the CM1 implementation for computational efficiency and parallel execution.
Evaluate against WRF and use diurnal and idealized convection simulations to investigate atmospheric responses.
evidence_signal: Comparisons with WRF show close agreement in wind-speed deficits and TKE enhancement, while diurnal simulations reproduce known stability-dependent boundary layer responses.
watch_item: The convection findings come from idealized simulations; the abstract reports no observational validation of downstream storm initiation.
paper_title: A Fitch-Based Wind Farm Parameterization for CM1: Implementation, Validation, and Impacts on Convection Initiation
